stories.title: Williams Equities’ Michael T. Cohen, Robert Getreu and Andrew Roos Take Manhattan
stories.excerpt: Williams Equities, a family-owned, New York City-focused commercial real estate firm run by Michael T. Cohen, Robert Getreu and Andrew Roos, marks its 100th anniversary this year. Despite the company’s centenarian status, the trio of principals operates a portfolio largely in its prime, energized by a youthful wave of tech companies flooding Midtown South and an overall vigorous Manhattan office market. Cohen, Getreu and Roos are second- or third-generation leaders of the company, originally established in 1926 by Victor Cohen as Williams & Company. The fledgling brokerage firm acquired its first property in 1953, and its portfolio grew to 2.1 million square feet by the end of the decade. Williams went on to establish strategic partnerships with Roos and Getreu’s predecessors, and their mounting acquisitions included 1700 Broadway, 1 Dag Hammarskjold Plaza and 28-40 West 23rd Street. The 1990s saw then-Williams Real Estate Company transform into a leasing and brokerage operation, GVA Williams — a bid to stay competitive in an institutionalizing real estate world. The entity was sold in 2008 to what would become Colliers’ New York office. “We wanted to manage assets, not people,” Roos told Commercial Observer. Williams Equities now operates as a business within a business, and Cohen, Getreu and Roos all hold senior posts at Colliers. Williams Equities separately owns and manages its 14-property portfolio, made up of 12 directly owned and two affiliated buildings. Colliers afforded the family business a heightened platform and market insights, as well as fabulous Bryant Park views from 1114 Avenue of the Americas. From that lofty perch, the principals oversee an office portfolio largely concentrated in Midtown South, a submarket that recently enjoyed its strongest first half-year of leasing since 2002, according to Colliers data, with tech-driven demand up 20 percent over the two quarters. The firm's office-focused portfolio benefits from strong leasing momentum driven by younger tech firms. However, the article is primarily a corporate profile and offers limited specifics on new leasing volume, pricing, or supply dynamics.
stories.impact: Limited direct relevance to multifamily development. The tech influx into Midtown South may signal broader job growth and Manhattan residency demand, but this article focuses on office landlords, not residential supply or rent trends. Monitor whether sustained tech hiring creates downstream residential demand in Manhattan submarkets.

stories.title: Broadview Reveals Plans for 32-Story Houston Office Tower
stories.excerpt: Broadview Real Estate unveiled plans for O27, a proposed 32-story office tower on Westheimer, just down the street from the River Oaks District. Designed by STG Design, the building will encompass more than 520,000 square feet of office space. Realty News Reports completion is anticipated in 2028. STG Design was the executive architect for Austin’s Block 185, the curved “Sail Tower” that serves as the home of Google’s Austin headquarters on the shores of Lady Bird Lake in downtown Austin. Named for its ZIP code, O27 is proposed for a 1.66-acre site at 4701 Westheimer. It is across from the soon-to-open Greenleigh, a redevelopment of the former Hotel Derek, and down the street from Highland Village shopping center. The O27 building site currently houses a former Extended Stay America hotel, which closed last year. Broadview Real Estate’s development pipeline exceeds 3 million square feet. bullets: Broadview Real Estate proposes O27, 32-story, 520K SF office tower on Westheimer, Houston

stories.summary: Broadview Real Estate is developing O27, a 520,000-square-foot office tower in Houston's Westheimer corridor near River Oaks, with completion slated for 2028. The site replaces a closed Extended Stay America hotel. The developer's broader pipeline tops 3 million square feet, signaling confidence in Sun Belt office fundamentals, though the market has cooled post-pandemic.
stories.impact: Office conversion of hospitality asset in Houston signals adaptive reuse opportunity; however, office development momentum in 2028 delivery window may face headwinds from ongoing remote work and elevated cap rates. More relevant: the hotel closure and land redevelopment could improve surrounding submarkets for mixed-use or multifamily infill near River Oaks. Monitor whether office failures drive hospitality-to-residential conversions in similar Houston corridors.

stories.title: ACORE Capital Refis 511 Fifth Avenue With $46M Loan
stories.excerpt: A joint venture involving Wharton Properties, Aurora Capital Associates and ACHS Management has secured a $45.5 million loan to refinance a Midtown Manhattan office property, Commercial Observer has learned. Acore Capital supplied the nonrecourse loan for the sponsorship’s 18-story office building at 511 Fifth Avenue that was recently redeveloped with 16,000 square feet of renovated space. The 1918-built property at the corner of Fifth Avenue and 43rd Street has seen leasing momentum of late with recent two-floor deals signed by GE Aerospace and WeWork along with a 9,812-square-foot lease from French consulting firm Wavestone. Meridian Capital Group negotiated the debt with a team led by Aaron Birnbaum. “The sponsorship team have done an exceptional job repositioning 511 Fifth Avenue, and the leasing results speak for themselves,” Birnbaum, co-founder and executive vice president at Meridian, said in a statement. “With new tenants signing while the loan was in process, our focus was keeping ACORE and the sponsors moving in lockstep as the rent roll grew.” Located a block north of the New York Public Library’s main building, 511 Fifth has amenities on the 15th floor that include a lounge, a juice bar and a fitness center. North Face, a global outdoor brand, opened a two-story, 21,000-square-foot flagship store at the base of the tower in November 2025. Spokespeople for ACORE Capital, Wharton Properties, Aurora Capital Associates and Achs Management did not immediately return requests for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: ACORE Capital closes $45.5M refi for 511 Fifth Avenue, 18-story Midtown Manhattan office, 1918-built
Recent leases: GE Aerospace, WeWork (two floors), Wavestone (9.8K SF); 16K SF renovated
Wharton Properties, Aurora Capital, ACHS Management JV; nonrecourse debt reflects improving leasing momentum
stories.summary: A joint venture led by Wharton Properties refinanced 511 Fifth Avenue, a historic 18-story Midtown office building, with a $45.5 million loan from ACORE Capital. The property has demonstrated strong leasing momentum with recent deals from GE Aerospace, WeWork, and Wavestone following a 16,000-square-foot renovation. Nonrecourse financing terms suggest lender confidence in the asset's recovery.
stories.impact: Manhattan office stabilization—particularly trophy Midtown properties near Fifth Avenue—signals improving underwriting conditions for office refinance. However, this is office-focused; relevance to multifamily is indirect: if Manhattan office recovers, it attracts high-income tenants to residential, supporting luxury and Class A rental demand in Midtown and surrounding submarkets. Refinance activity at modest LTVs ($45.5M on stabilized asset) shows capital returning to office, not flowing to multifamily development.

stories.title: DC Partners Inks $68.3M C-PACE Loan for Fredericksburg Mixed-Use Project
stories.excerpt: Nuveen Green Capital (NGC) closed on $68.6 million in C-PACE financing, administered through the Texas PACE Authority (TPA), for the ground-up construction of The Meuse, a mixed-use development in Fredericksburg, Texas. The town is about 70 miles northwest of San Antonio. DC Partners is the project developer. The two-part financing comprises $53.2 million for a hotel, Kimpton Fredericksburg, and $15.4 million for The Meuse’s retail component. Once complete, the property will be the city’s first combined hotel-and-retail destination. Located at the corner of U.S. Highway 290 and Main Street, The Meuse is a 22-acre development anchored by the Kimpton Fredericksburg Hotel, featuring approximately 13,000 square feet of meeting and event space, destination food-and-beverage offerings, resort-style amenities, and access to the global IHG reservation platform. The project’s 70,000-square-foot retail district will feature shops, markets, tasting rooms, and dining. The Meuse is slated to open in late 2027. stories.summary: Nuveen Green Capital provided $68.6 million in C-PACE financing for The Meuse, a mixed-use development in Fredericksburg, Texas by DC Partners. The project comprises a Kimpton-branded hotel ($53.2M financed) and 70,000 square feet of retail ($15.4M financed), opening late 2027. The 22-acre site at Highway 290 and Main Street will serve as Fredericksburg's first combined hotel-retail destination.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily development. The project is hotel- and retail-centric with C-PACE (energy efficiency) financing. However, mixed-use development in Fredericksburg signals secondary-market investment appetite in Texas Hill Country tourism corridor. If destination retail and hospitality succeed, follow-on demand for workforce and service-sector multifamily could emerge in Fredericksburg or nearby San Antonio markets.

stories.title: Endeavor Closes on $210M Texas-Centric CRE Fund
stories.excerpt: Endeavor Real Estate Group, an Austin-based investment and development firm, closed a $210 million private equity fund. Fund managers say the fund will have a particular focus on Texas. The fund will also be invested in a handful of other Sun Belt towns, such as Nashville, Charlotte and Salt Lake City. The $210 million fund is anticipated to support more than $3.0 billion in aggregate capitalization when combined with anticipated leverage and co-investment capital, subject to investment activity and market conditions. The Fund received strong support from new and existing investors, including national insurance firms, a large Texas-based endowment and other private investors. The Fund intends to pursue a value-add investment strategy by creating a portfolio of diverse real estate assets across various sectors, including but not limited to the acquisition or development of multi-family, retail, student housing, hospitality, industrial and mixed-use properties. The Fund anticipates making 30 to 40 investments, each sourced and executed by Endeavor.  The post Endeavor Closes on $210M Texas-Centric CRE Fund appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Endeavor Real Estate Group closes $210M Texas-focused private equity fund with $3B+ projected capitalization
Fund targets TX, Nashville, Charlotte, Salt Lake City; 30-40 planned investments across multifamily, retail, industrial, hospitality
Support from national insurers, large Texas endowment, private investors; value-add strategy
stories.summary: Endeavor Real Estate Group, an Austin-based firm, closed a $210 million private equity fund with projected capitalization exceeding $3 billion when leveraged and co-invested. The fund focuses on Texas and Sun Belt markets (Nashville, Charlotte, Salt Lake City) and plans 30–40 value-add investments across multifamily, retail, industrial, hospitality, and mixed-use assets. Strong support from institutional and Texas-based investors signals robust capital formation in the region.
stories.impact: Significant capital availability for multifamily acquisition and value-add repositioning in Texas and Sun Belt metros—Endeavor's explicit multifamily focus and $3B capitalization indicate aggressive deployment into Texas markets (Austin, Dallas, Houston, San Antonio) and secondary Sun Belt markets. This signals competitive bidding environment for multifamily assets and potential for new capital to chase yield in class-B/C repositioning. Developers should expect tighter cap rates and more sophisticated operators entering local markets; refinance and stabilized-hold opportunities may face higher valuations.

stories.title: Blackstone’s 2021 $1.3B CMBS Multifamily Loan Hits Special Servicing
stories.excerpt: The Sun Belt multifamily distress hampering apartment owners who borrowed before interest rates spiked has hit a private equity giant. A $1.3 billion Blackstone commercial mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) loan with a $517.7 million balance issued in fall 2021 has entered special servicing after missing its October 2026 maturity date, according to a Morningstar Credit alert issued Oct. 19. The BX 2021-21M Mortgage Trust deal was originally collateralized by 21 multifamily properties encompassing 6,671 units in Texas, Florida, Georgia, Washington, Colorado, South Carolina and Kansas. The CMBS loan’s portfolio is now six properties totaling 1,842 units, including two properties in Seattle along with apartment complexes in San Antonio, Jonesboro, Ga., and Bradenton, Fla., according to The Real Deal, which first reported the special servicing. Blackstone was granted a three-month forbearance to allow for the sale of the remaining assets in the loan, according to Morningstar. David Putro, associate managing director at Morningstar, said the remaining properties in the portfolio are generating “slightly more” cash flow than they were underwritten at, according to special servicer commentary. Barclays and Morgan Stanley co-originated the CMBS transaction, which was structured as a floating-rate, interest-only first-lien mortgage loan. Blackstone acquired the portfolio through multiple off-market, all-cash acquisitions from April through September 2021, according to a Fitch Ratings commentary at the time of the deal. Blacktone did not immediately return a request for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Blackstone's $1.3B CMBS loan (BX 2021-21M) defaults; $517.7M balance enters special servicing post-Oct 2026 maturity
Portfolio shrunk from 21 to 6 properties (1,842 units) across TX, FL, GA, WA, CO, SC, KS
Remaining properties: two Seattle, plus San Antonio, Jonesboro GA, Bradenton FL; three-month forbearance granted
stories.summary: A $1.3 billion CMBS loan originated by Blackstone in fall 2021 has entered special servicing after missing its October 2026 maturity. The loan's multifamily portfolio has been reduced from 21 properties (6,671 units) to 6 properties (1,842 units) across Sun Belt and non-Sun Belt markets. Remaining collateral includes two Seattle properties and complexes in San Antonio, Jonesboro, and Bradenton. Blackstone received a three-month forbearance to facilitate asset sales.
stories.impact: Major signal of multifamily distress in Sun Belt markets, particularly Texas and Florida, where 2021-vintage floating-rate debt now faces massive rate headwinds and occupancy/NOI pressure. Forced liquidation of Blackstone's portfolio in San Antonio, Jonesboro, and Bradenton could pressure rent and cap rates in those markets. For developers: monitor distressed sales in Texas and Florida for acquisition opportunities; refinance windows are tightening for non-stabilized assets. Seattle exposure signals Western markets also affected. Expect continued special servicing and CMBS losses through 2026–2027.

stories.title: 30-Acre Vero Beach Waterfront Property Hits the Market
stories.excerpt: Cushman & Wakefield has been retained by investor John Devaney to market two adjoining waterfront properties on Vero Beach’s north barrier island. Cushman & Wakefield Virgilio Fernandez is leading the marketing effort on behalf of Devaney. The sites can be purchased together or separately. The listing price for the two properties is over $60 million. The Grand Oceanfront & River Estate, located at 12906 Jimmy Buffett Memorial Highway, encompasses approximately 14.84 acres, including 8.63 acres of buildable upland stretching from the Atlantic Ocean to the Indian River Lagoon and 6.21 acres of privately owned submerged land. The neighboring River Peninsula Estate, located at 12505 Jimmy Buffett Memorial Highway, totals approximately 15.44 acres, including 8.33 acres of upland and 7.11 acres of privately owned submerged land.  The sites may offer opportunities for condominium development and private marina uses, subject to applicable approvals and entitlements. Additional density could potentially be pursued through planned residential development approval or a future land use amendment.    The post 30-Acre Vero Beach Waterfront Property Hits the Market appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: 30-acre waterfront Vero Beach property listed for $60M+; two adjoining sites (Grand Oceanfront & River Peninsula Estate)
14.84 acres and 15.44 acres respectively; combined buildable upland ~16.96 acres plus submerged land

stories.summary: Cushman & Wakefield is marketing two adjoining waterfront properties totaling approximately 30 acres in Vero Beach, Florida for $60 million+. The Grand Oceanfront & River Estate (14.84 acres) and River Peninsula Estate (15.44 acres) each span the Atlantic Ocean to the Indian River Lagoon with private submerged land. The sites offer potential for condominium development and private marina uses, though subject to regulatory approvals.
stories.impact: Limited relevance to rental multifamily development. The property is pitched toward condo/fractional ownership and marinas, not apartment development. However, Vero Beach waterfront land sales signal South Florida investment appetite in secondary coastal markets. If condo market softens, the land could be repositioned for rental multifamily. Monitor Vero Beach and coastal Florida for conversion opportunities if condo absorption slows.

stories.title: New Red Oak Rental Community Debuts with Onsite Fishing Pond
stories.excerpt: Greystar, in partnership with Whitman Peterson has opened Halden at Red Oak, a new apartment community in Red Oak, TX. Halden at Red Oak offers a unique amenity: an on-site fishing pond. The city of Red Oak asked Greystar to preserve and improve the existing pond for public use, and it now includes piers and a paved trail that loops around the water. Additional amenities include a 24/7 fitness center, a pool with a tanning shelf, an outdoor terrace with a fire pit, and an outdoor kitchen for grilling and dining. Halden at Red Oak offers one- and two-bedroom apartments and three- and four-bedroom single-family homes for rent. Residences include personal patios or balconies and large fenced-in yards. Halden at Red Oak sits just off Highway 342, about 20 miles south of downtown Dallas. The site includes two future retail spaces. The post New Red Oak Rental Community Debuts with Onsite Fishing Pond appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Greystar + Whitman Peterson open Halden at Red Oak, multifamily + single-family rental community south of Dallas
Mixed product: 1-2 BR apartments, 3-4 BR single-family rentals; on-site fishing pond, pool, fitness, fire pit

stories.summary: Greystar and Whitman Peterson have opened Halden at Red Oak, a mixed-product rental community in Red Oak, Texas (20 miles south of Dallas) combining apartments (1–2 bedroom) and single-family homes (3–4 bedroom) for rent. Amenities include an on-site fishing pond (public-private partnership with city), pool, fitness center, fire pit, and outdoor kitchen. Two future retail spaces are included on the site.
stories.impact: Positive signal of rental multifamily supply expansion in Dallas south submarket (Red Oak). Mixed-product strategy (apartments + single-family rentals) reflects developer confidence in suburban Dallas rental demand and diversified tenant base. The public amenity (fishing pond) demonstrates developer commitment to placemaking and community buy-in, potentially enabling faster lease-up and premium rents. For competitors: expect continued supply growth in Dallas suburbs 15–25 miles from downtown; monitor absorption and rent trends in Red Oak and nearby Midlothian, Arlington submarkets.

stories.title: New York Office Tenant Improvement Totals Rise in 2026 Amid Market Shifts
stories.excerpt: Manhattan tenant improvement (TI) allowances — costs that commercial landlords cover for tenants to remodel spaces — have dramatically evolved since the pandemic. Gone are the days in which these allowances functioned as a simple deal sweetener to entice the city’s white-shoe law firms and digital media startups. Instead, brokers and landlords say it is a structural — albeit costly — necessity in today’s deal-making. Since 2019, TI allowances across the Manhattan office market have increased 59.2 percent, according to Avison Young data based on 12-month moving averages. TI allowances peaked in 2024 amid citywide office vacancies. After a substantial dip in 2025, this particular concession is back on the rise, up 7.9 percent year-over-year to $120.80 per square foot in September, according to Avison Young’s data. The upticks are documented across every Manhattan submarket and in top-performing asset classes. Yet, rising construction costs and tenant standards, as well as an interest rate hike and surging Treasury yields, have added more pricing pressure to the sought-after perk. Meanwhile, months of free rent, another popular concession from commercial landlords, fell this year by 8.6 percent compared to 2025, hovering as of October at just over 10 months per lease on average. The rise in TI allowances and the dip in free rent diverges from the usual trend, said Vikrant Ghate, Avison Young’s New York City manager for market intelligence. Typically, high interest rates would trigger an uptick in free rent, Ghate said, while capital concessions like TI allowances stabilize or decline. bullets: Manhattan office TI allowances up 59.2% since 2019; peaked 2024, dipped 2025, rebounded +7.9% YoY to $120.80/SF in Sept 2026
Rising TI costs driven by construction inflation, elevated interest rates, surging Treasury yields, tenant standards
Documented across all Manhattan submarkets and top asset classes; TI now structural necessity, not deal sweetener
stories.summary: Manhattan office tenant improvement allowances have surged 59.2% since 2019, reaching $120.80 per square foot in September 2026—up 7.9% year-over-year after a 2025 dip. TI costs have become a structural necessity rather than a discretionary concession, driven by rising construction costs, higher interest rates, and elevated tenant expectations. The trend spans all Manhattan submarkets and premium asset classes.
stories.impact: Reflects underlying office market weakness and landlord desperation to secure tenants in competitive Manhattan market. Rising TI costs compress landlord NOI and increase development underwriting risk for office projects. For multifamily: rising construction costs (cited as TI cost driver) also affect apartment development feasibility and pro-forma returns. Developers should model 2026–2027 construction cost inflation and monitor whether office TI pressures spill into multifamily construction labor and materials markets in NYC.

stories.title: StageLynk Launches AI Booking Platform for Film and TV Stages
stories.excerpt: StageLynk has launched an AI-powered studio search and production planning platform for the film and television industry. The Los Angeles-based startup, which also has an office in Chicago, spent several years developing a soundstage booking platform to connect studio owners and production companies. The platform provides a searchable soundstage directory with nearly 17 million square feet of inventory across 1,200 soundstages in major production hubs such as Los Angeles, New York, Atlanta, Vancouver, Toronto and the U.K. Finding the right soundstage can require calls, emails, spreadsheets and repeated outreach to determine which facilities best fit a project. StageLynk said it condenses that process into one platform. “The product is a marketplace to connect studio facilities with productions,” said Brett Robbins, who with Will Krug co-founded StageLynk. “For those two sides to find each other, interact and transact. The entertainment industry has shifted over the last few years, and so the product has expanded in its scope relative to where we initially set out.” The platform includes StageScout, StageLynk’s AI-powered production assistant, which helps production teams evaluate factors beyond just the stage itself. Those factors include state and regional tax incentives, permitting requirements, union considerations, local production information and nearby amenities. “It goes beyond just, if I’m a producer, what facilities might I be able to find to film my production project?” Robbins explained. “And it incorporates all the other important items that go into decision-making on where something is filmed and how that can go beyond the four walls of the physical real estate — things like state incentives, surrounding amenities and physical location shoots. bullets: StageLynk launches AI platform for soundstage booking; 17M SF inventory across 1,200 stages in major production hubs

The platform aggregates ~17 million square feet of inventory across 1,200 soundstages in Los Angeles, New York, Atlanta, Vancouver, Toronto, and the U.K., streamlining the booking process and production planning.
